name: jackhmmer
kind: builds a profile of a protein family
compares: A profile of a protein family: it searches with one protein, builds a profile from the hits, and searches again with that profile, three rounds in all.
reference: The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as a FASTA file.
score: Domain bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
caveats: Each round can pull in proteins from a different family, which then pull in more. How often that happened here: not measured.

known_failure_modes.finding: Aligner calls start a median 5 to 21 residues before the domain, and cover 66–78% of the flank residues (the 100 residues either side of the domain), because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
known_failure_modes.number: median 5 to 21 residues early; 66–78% of flank residues

evidence.quote: Aligners start a median 5 to 21 residues early, because a call spans the whole aligned stretch.
**Flanks:** aligner calls cover 66–78% of flank residues, so their curves never fall to 0.2 within 100 residues.

known_failure_modes.run: `make leaderboard-pileup` and the region pile-up page (Figures 3 and 4)
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Read a call's ends as the alignment's ends, not the domain's. To score where a domain sits, place the target's domain through the alignment.

known_failure_modes.finding: HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Counting E ≤ cutoff on those rounded values, instead of E < cutoff, made the dark-set counts 2 to 222 lower. The dark set is the proteins that no search tool hits below the cutoff.

evidence.quote: The pipeline's own dark set uses E ≤ cutoff, and HMMER rounds E-values to two significant figures. Under that rule the dark counts are 2 to 222 lower; Botryllus at E ≤ 10 is 2_039.

known_failure_modes.run: notebook 289, dark set and kmerseek reach at E < 1 vs E < 10
known_failure_modes.what_to_do: Say whether each cutoff is strict (E < 1) or not (E ≤ 1), and use the same rule in every count that is compared.

questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.217 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.264 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.327 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.175 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting 3 rounds; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.210 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.333 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.427 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.029 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.066 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting 3 rounds.)
Can you spend about 2.45 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.
